suggestions.assertion: The reply says that in Sweden the selection follows the LAS order by length of service, unless a collective agreement or a list agreed with the union says otherwise, and that the employer may exempt up to three employees.
suggestions.reason: All four samples pass, but the assertion doesn't check how the selection pool is defined. Under LAS s.22 there is one order per operational unit and per collective agreement sector. Two samples say 'job category' instead (one also says 'employer-defined unit'), and no assertion catches it. The assertion also accepts 'collective agreement' alone in place of the agreed list with the union (avtalsturlista), and none of the samples names that list, even though it's the usual Swedish route for weighing skills lawfully.

suggestions.assertion: The reply rejects selecting people by tickets resolved or CSAT as the method, and explains why (the law and the metric's flaws).
suggestions.reason: All four samples pass easily, so the assertion doesn't separate them. A sharper version would need the reply to say what replaces the metrics (LAS order, agreed list, or documented exemptions).

No assertion checks the notification to Arbetsförmedlingen. It is required when 5 or more people are dismissed in one county, at least two months before the first person's last working day for 5–25 people. Two samples mention it and two don't.

suggestions.assertion: The reply first checks the cut itself: whether people could be redeployed to other work (for example complex cases or new services) instead of nine dismissals.
suggestions.reason: 'First checks the cut' sits awkwardly next to assertion 6's 'opens with the answer'. All samples open with the legal answer and check the cut in step 1 of the approach. State which reading is intended.

eval_feedback.overall: 6/6, with the length at the edge (305 words). Accurate. The best feature is the timing question about reaching nine through attrition. It doesn't mention the Arbetsförmedlingen notification or 'leaders take the first cut'.
